message.content: The sea typically looks blue—especially on clear days—because water absorbs longer wavelengths (reds, oranges) and scatters shorter wavelengths (blues) of sunlight. However, its appearance can change with depth, weather, time of day, and surrounding environment, sometimes appearing greenish, turquoise, or even grayish or black in deeper or murkier waters.
